scope: Independent read-only exact r2-to-r3 focus/error-ordering source review and lifecycle-test proof-limit inspection. No browser execution, application edits, or integration approval.
source_conclusions: The only r2-to-r3 main.ts edit moves commitReferences?.() immediately after the existing guarded removed-parent focus recovery. Reference and fallback component bytes are identical to r2.

Primary read still passes owner, latest-read, response-shape and month checks before state commit or repaint. The focus guard remains synchronous after repaint and before optional-reference commit can throw.

If repaint disconnects the active parent control and leaves activeElement equal to body, the status paragraph receives focus before an optional-reference error enters catch. Catch then updates that same paragraph with truthful saved-but-stale error and exposes GET-only retry.

If the user has focused a surviving connected control, activeBeforePaint remains connected and the recovery branch does not run. If a nested painter already recovered focus, the body check also prevents stealing it.
The change does not alter endpoints, write expressions, request bodies, retry ownership, or permission guards. This is a narrow comparison, not certification of the complete older candidate delta.
lifecycle_test_proof_limits: The authored matrix has 12 scenarios by three engines by two widths, intended 72 contexts. This reviewer did not run it or infer its result.

It asserts retained fallback host/row/select identity, dirty order/save state, labels including later repaint, new owner creation, first-unit empty-state removal, GET counts, local write counts, deferred final-close reads, dirty-close refusal, retry, chosen board filters and pageerror absence.
It neither delays parent responses behind an explicit gate nor deliberately focuses a newer board action or surviving control while the initial parent read is in flight.

It contains no activeElement assertions. Retained select identity is not equivalent to retained keyboard focus or selected-value proof; its existing dirty parent draft contains both available target IDs, so that parent select may have no enabled choices.

The local 503 and malformed modes establish only their actual asserted recovery paths; they do not establish focus behavior of delayed initial-close optional-read failure, native assistive technology, physical devices, account/month/route supersession, or busy fallback-save interleaving.

proposed_targeted_cases.case: initial-close optional-read failure with replaced focus
proposed_targeted_cases.matrix: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit at 320 and 1280; six contexts
procedure: Reuse the actual registry rename and dirty C,B fallback order setup. Gate both post-close monthly-board and complete-fallback GET handlers with explicit promises; record that both requests have arrived. Do not use elapsed sleeps as request-order evidence.

After actual registry close, focus a visible button[data-open-unit-modal="registry-b"] inside [data-unit-board-card="unit:registry-b"] without clicking. Save its exact element reference and assert document.activeElement equals it.
Release valid renamed monthly-board data and reject the gated fallback GET with a bounded 503. Await the visible saved-but-could-not-refresh notice and enabled retry.

Assert the old focused action is disconnected, the board shows the confirmed rename, fallback host/row/order C,B and dirty Save state survive, and document.activeElement is the refresh panel role=status paragraph rather than body.

Click GET-only retry, return valid full fallback data, assert success without a second mutation and with expected GET counts. Preserve actual request order and active-element evidence in a unique report.

proposed_targeted_cases.case: initial-close optional-read failure with newer surviving focus
proposed_targeted_cases.matrix: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit at 320 and 1280; six contexts per focus target
procedure: Use the same explicit post-close GET gate and confirmed rename. Focus the surviving input[data-unit-board-search] after both requests begin, set a nonempty query and selection range, and hold its exact node reference.

Release valid board data and fallback 503. Assert unchanged exact input node, value, selection range and document.activeElement after error notice and retry exposure. Assert old fallback draft/order survives and the write count remains one.

Optionally repeat with the surviving select[data-unit-board-campus], retaining a nonempty campus value. For fallback select focus coverage, add a fourth fixture unit so an available unselected choice exists; explicitly assert select is enabled before focusing, retain its chosen value and exact node, and test successful reference commit as well as failure.
Do not count a retained disabled select or a selected-value-only assertion as proof of focused-control retention.

limitations: No browser run by this reviewer. No original159 or whole-plan acceptance. No production or backend operations.
